answer: An operator running ten clones fails this check because memory is costly to fake. Each identity strings its peer-attested answers like a private pearl necklace, one pearl per epoch, and drops each pearl's hash into a public lagoon of commitments so none can be rewritten. Random peers quiz it on its own old pearls and on another identity's; knowing a stranger's private pearls proves shared control and strikes both. Rewards stay frozen in tundra until five quizzes pass, so each extra clone needs its own stream of distinct, attested work, kept strictly apart.
